overall: At 1:00 AM ET, Atlanta is in its overnight cooling phase with the current temperature at 71.6°F and falling at -1.8°F/hr, well below the running max of 73.4°F. The flat running max trend (all readings locked at 73.4°F) confirms no meaningful heating has occurred yet, consistent with the early overnight hour. The moderate dewpoint of 57.2°F and calm winds suggest a setup that could support meaningful afternoon heating once the sun drives the boundary layer.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable disagreement among the models, with GFS running aggressively at 90.3°F while ECMWF (84.7°F) and NBM (83.3°F) cluster about 6–7°F lower. The ensemble signals reinforce skepticism toward the upper end: the even model places only a 5% chance on the 90–91°F bin and the odd model puts just 19% on 87–88°F, with both flagged as Tier 4 (Avoid), suggesting the GFS solution is an outlier.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence points toward a high in the mid-80s, anchored by the ECMWF/NBM consensus and reinforced by the ensemble models assigning low probability to outcomes above 87°F. Calm winds and moderate moisture are mildly supportive of heating, but the ensemble distribution tilts decidedly away from the GFS's aggressive upper-80s/low-90s scenario. Confidence is moderate — there is real model spread, but the probabilistic signals clearly favor the lower end of the guidance envelope around 84–85°F.
